annotation.authors_or_issuer: UK National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC); US CISA; FBI and international partner agencies
key_provisions_or_claims: Security must be a core requirement across the whole AI system life cycle, following secure-by-default and secure-by-design principles.
Four stages: secure design, secure development, secure deployment, and secure operation and maintenance.
Providers should take responsibility for security outcomes of downstream users and inform them of unmitigated risks.
Threat modelling, supply chain due diligence, asset protection and documentation (model cards, SBOMs).
Incident response plans, red teaming before release, monitoring and information sharing.
annotation.summary_en: Joint international guidelines led by the UK NCSC and US CISA, with many partner agencies, on secure AI system development. They cover secure design, development, deployment, and operation and maintenance for providers of machine-learning systems, using a secure-by-design approach and addressing adversarial ML, supply chain, and incident management.
annotation.title_clean: Guidelines for secure AI system development
